title: Remove deprecated time-cap fields from JetBrains task parsing
description: Objective: finish JetBrains's deprecated task time-budget retirement after the UI consumers have landed. Deliverable: the client Task model and both JSON parsing paths ignore legacy time-budget payloads while retaining all live runtime metrics and limits. Exact scope: moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt (remove TaskBudget and Task.budget plus stale surface comment), moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/MoeJson.kt (remove import, parseTaskBudget helper and BOTH parseTasks/parseTask assignments), moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeProjectService.kt (comment-only: replace 'short budget' retry-window wording), and moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/util/MoeJsonTest.kt. Add red-first parser equality regressions: the same task with/without populated legacy budget JSON parses identically through snapshot and single-task APIs; old code must differ because it populates Task.budget. Also cover absent/null/malformed legacy values while preserving metrics, reopen/step data and error handling for malformed unrelated fields. The UI prerequisite removes the old typed consumers before this field disappears; do not import or construct TaskBudget in new tests. NOT in scope: daemon schema/data rewrites, daemon deprecation notes, chat hop limits, reopen caps, startup timing behavior, or presentation changes beyond the prerequisite. Exact gate from repository root on Windows: & .\moe-jetbrains\gradlew.bat -p moe-jetbrains test; exit $LASTEXITCODE. Unix: (cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test). The parent's final guard will run case-insensitive budget grep over all src/main. Coordinate shared Gradle output use; preserve foreign files.
definitionOfDone: TaskBudget, Task.budget and budget-specific parser code/imports are absent from JetBrains main sources; both parseTasks and parseTask ignore the legacy field.

JUnit fixtures assert identical parsed live task/metrics data with absent, populated, null and malformed legacy budget values through both parser paths; populated-field equality fails before the removal.
No case-insensitive budget text remains in moe-jetbrains/src/main after this task and its UI prerequisite, including comment-only leftovers; unrelated startup retry behavior is unchanged.
TaskMetrics durations, reopen/step counters and all live client limits remain intact and tested.
Full JetBrains Gradle test gate passes with positive test counts, including the UI prerequisite tests unchanged.
taskRails: Keep scope to the four named files and retain error handling for unrelated malformed JSON.
Do not remove the daemon's legacy-field deprecation notes or alter persisted task data.
Do not weaken the prerequisite's production-presentation tests.

implementationPlan.description: VERIFY THE UI PREREQUISITE IS GONE BEFORE DELETING WHAT IT CONSUMED. Read-only, no edits. (a) Prove task-0471536723384823995c88fe0fb58e15 landed: epicSiblings landing.merged true, or `git log <branch> --grep "Moe-Task: task-0471536723384823995c88fe0fb58e15"`. It was still PLANNING on 2026-09-11, so re-measure. (b) Independently confirm no consumer is left, because a stale reader is what turns this removal into a compile break: `grep -rn "task.budget\|TaskBudget" moe-jetbrains/src/main` must return only the three lines this task owns - the data class at Models.kt:115-119, the property at Models.kt:168, and MoeJson.kt's import at line 22, helper at 357 and the two call sites at 330 and 491. Today board/TaskCard.kt also reads task.budget at 357-392 through its buildBudgetBadge helper; if those are still present, the prerequisite has not landed and you must moe.report_blocked naming its id rather than deleting the badge yourself - that badge belongs to the prerequisite. (c) Note two facts that keep this removal clean: getLongOrNull at MoeJson.kt:77 has four other callers in the metrics parsers, so it stays; and MoeJsonTest.kt currently contains no budget reference at all, so there is no existing test to rewrite, only new ones to add. (d) Record foreign dirty paths and preserve them. Own only the four named files.

RED FIRST, WITHOUT NAMING THE TYPE YOU ARE ABOUT TO DELETE. Add regressions to moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/util/MoeJsonTest.kt, preserving every existing test unchanged. The central assertion is an equality one: build two JSON payloads identical except that one carries a populated legacy time-budget object, parse both through MoeJson.parseState and again through MoeJson.parseTask, and assert the two resulting Task values are equal. That fails on today's code, which populates the field from one payload and not the other, and it passes once the field is gone - a genuine red on the old behavior, which the epic rail requires. Crucially, write it WITHOUT importing or constructing the legacy type: compare parsed Task objects, never the removed class, so the same test compiles before and after the removal. Add the shape variants around it - the legacy key absent, explicitly null, and malformed as a string, a number and an array - each asserting the same equality and, in the same assertions, that the live data survives untouched: TaskMetrics durations, reopenCount, step data, comments and identity. Add one control that keeps error handling honest for unrelated malformed input: a task whose legacy field is malformed AND whose unrelated fields include a wrong-typed value still parses into a usable task through both paths, proving this removal did not make the parser brittle. Coordinate exclusive shared Gradle use, then run the focused class - Windows from the repository root `& .\moe-jetbrains\gradlew.bat -p moe-jetbrains test --tests com.moe.util.MoeJsonTest; exit $LASTEXITCODE`, Unix `(cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test --tests com.moe.util.MoeJsonTest)` - and save the failing output. It must be an assertion failure about unequal tasks, not a compile error.

REMOVE THE MODEL SURFACE. In moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt delete the TaskBudget data class at lines 115-119 and the `budget` property at line 168 from Task, and reword the surface comment at line 166 so it no longer names the removed concept - it currently reads as a shared comment for two fields, and the metrics half must survive while the wording loses the legacy term entirely, since a later step greps case-insensitively for it. Change nothing else in the file: HandoffNote, TaskMetrics, FailedDodItem, PlanCritiqueResult, planSizeWarnings, verification and reviewSummary all stay exactly as they are, and no parameter ordering moves except by the one deletion. Removing a defaulted property cannot break a named-argument call site, and the parser is the only place that passed it.

REMOVE THE PARSER SURFACE FROM BOTH PATHS. In moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/MoeJson.kt delete the import at line 22, the private parseTaskBudget helper at lines 357-370, and BOTH assignments - line 330 inside the private parseTasks used by parseState, and line 491 inside the public parseTask used for single-task messages. Both matter: leaving either behind would not compile, and forgetting that there are two Task constructors is the classic miss in this file. Do NOT touch getLongOrNull at line 77 - it still has four callers in the task-metrics and aggregate-metrics parsers. Leave every other helper, its permissiveness and its callers exactly as they are; this is a deletion, not a parser refactor, and unrelated malformed JSON must keep behaving as it does today. Re-run the focused test class from the previous step: the equality regressions must now pass, because an unknown JSON key is simply ignored.

CLEAR THE LAST TEXTUAL LEFTOVER AND PROVE IT. In moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeProjectService.kt line 190, reword the retry comment that currently reads "keep the original short budget before declaring failure" so it describes the retry window without the legacy term - the sentence is about a waiting period, not a task time cap. This is comment-only: do not touch scheduleRetryAttempt, the attempt counter, the delay, publishStatus or any startup timing behavior, which the task scope explicitly excludes. Then run the guard the parent will run: `grep -rni budget moe-jetbrains/src/main` must return nothing at all. If it reports a leftover in a file outside these four, that belongs to the UI prerequisite - report it rather than widening this task's scope to fix it.

FULL GATE, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, HANDOFF. (a) Acquire the shared Gradle slot through the Moe resource protocol and run the gate fresh from the repository root - Windows exactly `& .\moe-jetbrains\gradlew.bat -p moe-jetbrains test; exit $LASTEXITCODE`, Unix `(cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test)` - then release the slot either way. Require exit 0, real :test execution with freshly written JUnit XML and nonzero counts; an UP-TO-DATE result is not a test run, so re-run with a task-local rerun and then the exact unfiltered command again. Every pre-existing test must pass unchanged, and a task rail forbids weakening the UI prerequisite's presentation tests to get there - if one of them fails, that is a real finding, not something to edit away. Never cancel a peer's build or delete a shared cache. (b) Adversarially review the deletion: are BOTH parser call sites gone; does the model still carry metrics, handoffs, critique, plan-size warnings, verification and review summary; is getLongOrNull still present with its four callers; did any unrelated helper's permissiveness change; does an unknown legacy key in a payload still parse cleanly rather than throwing; is the case-insensitive grep genuinely clean across all of src/main; and did the service edit stay comment-only with startup retry behavior untouched. Confirm the daemon's own legacy-field deprecation notes and persisted task data were not touched - they are explicitly out of scope. (c) Complete through moe.complete_task with the exact command, exit code and counts, the saved red output from step 2 as the fails-on-old-behavior evidence, and every modified path in modifiedFiles. Note in the summary that this unblocks task-e7f534f147b74650ba06c2b98c022afb, which adds the blocker metadata fields to these same two files.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Writing the red test by constructing the legacy type and asserting it is no longer populated - rejected: that test would stop compiling the moment the type is deleted, so it could never run green. Comparing two parsed Task values instead keeps one test compiling on both sides of the change, which is what makes the red meaningful. Deleting getLongOrNull along with its former caller - rejected: four live callers remain. Removing the board badge here to avoid waiting on the prerequisite - rejected: it belongs to task-0471536723384823995c88fe0fb58e15 and taking it would both widen scope past four files and weaken that task's own tests, which a task rail forbids. Leaving the service comment alone as harmless prose - rejected: the Definition of Done requires a clean case-insensitive grep over all of src/main, so the wording has to go even though nothing executable changes.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured live on 2026-09-11. The removal is exactly five deletions plus one reword, and the only real hazard is ordering: TaskCard.kt still reads task.budget through buildBudgetBadge at lines 352-392, so deleting the model field before the UI prerequisite lands is a guaranteed compile break. That is why step 1 verifies the consumer is gone by grep rather than trusting the board column. Two facts keep the deletion tidy: getLongOrNull at MoeJson.kt:77 has four other callers in the task-metrics and aggregate-metrics parsers, so it is not orphaned and must not be removed; and MoeJsonTest.kt contains no budget reference today, so nothing existing needs rewriting. MoeJson has two independent Task constructors - the private parseTasks used by parseState and the public parseTask used for single-task messages - and both assign the field, which is the classic miss in this file. The service line is genuinely unrelated prose about a daemon startup retry window that merely happens to use the same word, and the Definition of Done's case-insensitive grep is what forces it into scope.
planningNotes.risks: Ordering is the whole risk: verify the UI consumer is gone before deleting the model field, or the module will not compile. Both parser call sites must go together. Do not let a deletion turn into a parser refactor - unrelated helpers keep their existing permissiveness, and an unknown legacy key in a payload must simply be ignored rather than rejected. The red must be an assertion failure about unequal parsed tasks, not a compile error, or it proves nothing. These two files are contended: the blocker-metadata task task-e7f534f147b74650ba06c2b98c022afb adds six fields to the same Models.kt and MoeJson.kt and is sequenced behind this one, so land cleanly and do not leave half-removed state. Gradle output is shared infrastructure here - serialize it, never clean a peer's cache, and treat an UP-TO-DATE result as no test run. Finally, if the final grep finds a leftover outside the four owned files, report it instead of widening.
